artdefs-DGloOU95.js.header: Brush art definitions: hold-to-charge and cooldown timings, which art each paint colour casts (fireball, ice lance, bounce orb, vine lash), each art's tuning, and the Ember and Frost Crest upgrades.

chests-Bz72fjJ7.js.header: Treasure chests for the sky islands and caverns: five chest styles merged into one mesh whose lids hinge open in the vertex shader. Handles the open prompt, the opening cinematic with light rays and bursts, loot, locks and the storm seal over the grand chest.

hints-Cuh7l1uz.js.header: Proximity hints: registered hint spots show their text as a UI prompt while the hero stands near the closest one, and hide it when the hero walks away.

ink-CyRBoTPw.js.header: Ink plants: a glowing plant species for each paint colour, instanced and swaying, with halo sprites above them. Walking into or interacting with a grown plant refills that ink as sparks fly to the hero, then the plant wilts and regrows.

index-D9AhHOn0.js.header: Game-wide constants every system imports: gravity, the four paint colours and their palette, island landmarks and special sites (dry meadow, boss arena, sky island, interior pockets), item and art definitions, and the Rapier collision groups.
Small event bus (on, once, off, emit) that the systems use to talk to each other.
Keyboard, mouse and gamepad input: action bindings, per-frame pressed and released state, move and look vectors, and pointer lock.

Shared shader uniforms (time, wind, sun, heightmap, paint volume, vitality and burn maps) and the wb_* GLSL chunks every material includes, with no-op paint and burn chunks until those systems install their own.
Registry that maps Rapier collider handles to what they belong to (kind, surface, object).
Interior manager for the caverns and temples: fades the hero in and out, hides the outdoor world while inside and switches to the interior's lighting.
Player settings (mouse sensitivity, quality, volumes, controls hint) loaded from and saved to localStorage.
The sixteen game systems: a lazy import for each one and the order boot creates them in.
Seeded random numbers, seeded simplex noise and fBm, and the clamp, lerp, smoothstep and damp helpers.
Minimal stand-ins for every system, used when one is stubbed out from the URL or fails to start: plain lighting, a simple heightmap island, an orbit-camera player and so on.
Boot: sets up the renderer, Rapier and the shared ctx, creates each system in order (falling back to its stub), warms up the shaders and runs the frame loop.

signals-DTd5o0VY.js.header: Per-context hero signal bus (air jumps, flame rings, frost patches) shared by the player, character and audio systems. Also computes how dark it is around the hero (caves, dim interiors, night), which drives the lantern.

skyground-b2tRwISP.js.header: Brush combat tuning shared by the player, character, UI and audio: attack moves, the three-hit combo, flurry, jump slash, spin charge, dodges and the Masterstroke counter after a perfect dodge. Also the item-reveal, Chroma Brush and Sky Mantle timings.
Ground queries that know about the sky island: its surface, terrain and water heights, water depth, and how strongly a point belongs to the Painted Aerie.

treeSpecies-BUQLnmez.js.header: Trims an instanced grass or flower ring to the grid cells the camera can actually see and returns how many instances to draw.
Paints the foliage texture atlas on a canvas: broadleaf and birch leaf clumps, fern and palm fronds.

Shared vegetation shading: field and paint uniforms, wind gust and leaf lighting GLSL, and the patch that turns a Lambert or depth material into a vegetation material. Also wraps a seeded random function with range, pick and chance helpers.
Tree shaders and materials: swaying foliage cards, three bark kinds, reeds and solid plants that react to wind, paint and fire.
Procedural plant geometry: a vertex builder with vegetation attributes, plus tubes along curves, leaf cards, fronds and leafy canopies.
Tree species grown from a seed: broadleaf, birch, conifer and palm, each returning trunk and foliage geometry plus its size.

util-B5nH5oxN.js.header: Pooled additive point-sprite particles: ballistic, homing, swirling and rising sparks for bursts, pickups and ink refills. Used by content, sky, temples and caverns.
Ambient motes: drifting pollen, blinking fireflies and rising embers scattered over areas as one additive point cloud animated in the vertex shader.

Shared content helpers: seeded randomness, procedural geometry (rounded boxes, lathes, temple columns, rocks, tapered tubes, vertex colours, merging), terrain placement queries, a soft glow sprite texture and a guard that logs failed build steps.

audio-poB4Ix8l.js.header: Sound synthesis toolkit for the procedural sound recipes: seeded random numbers, a state-variable filter, one-pole filters, pink and brown noise, and generators for tones, filtered noise, modal rings, grains, crackles, drips, bubbles and creaks. Also mixing and panning, tail trimming, loop crossfades and loudness normalisation.

Ambience sound recipes: seamless loops for wind, rushing water, fluttering, rustling grass, surf, lapping water, crickets, fire and sliding, plus wildlife calls (bird chirps, whistles, trills and warbles, a dove, an owl and frogs).
Synthesised instrument notes the musical sounds are built from: piano, celesta, harp and FM bell notes made of decaying partials, and brass and pad notes made of band-limited sawtooth oscillators.

Combat sound recipes: brush swings and the spin charge, hits for each paint colour, Smudge, Spitter and Brute noises, the attack telegraph and alert sting, and the hero's hurt, death, pickup, lock-on, perfect-dodge and flurry sounds. Defines the whoosh, ink splat, thump and formant voice helpers that later recipes reuse.

Greymaw's sound recipes (rising from the ink, roar, slam, sweep, ink rain, crystal, stagger, hurt and death), the boss barrier, chest and item-get fanfares, the elite sting and the elites' attack sounds. Built from a small orchestral kit: choir, timpani, cymbals, cached instrument notes, panned layers and early reflections.

Greymaw's sound recipes, the boss barrier, chest and item-get fanfares and the elites' attack sounds, plus the boss music samples (choir and brass notes at fixed roots, timpani, boom, anvil and gong) and the list that gathers every boss-fight recipe.

Sound recipes for the caverns and temples: cave, kiln and cistern ambience loops, the lantern hum and the cave reverb impulse, drips, chimes and kiln pops, the entry, puzzle, lantern, crest and Cloudstep stingers, and the double-jump puff, flame ring, frost crackle and lantern tinkle.

Brush art sound recipes for the four colours: seamless charge hums and the ready chimes, the cast and hit sounds of the fireball, ice lance, bounce orb and vine lash, the heavy hit and the fizzle when ink runs out.
Battle music samples: Karplus-Strong pizzicato notes across the pizz range, and the taiko, tom, clack, shaker, crash, swell and sting hits the battle music is sequenced from.

Highwind Perch and brushflight sound recipes: the perch socket, rumble, bloom, hum and claim, the wind, flutter, boost and paint loops heard while flying, the mount, dismount and boost one-shots, and the flute samples of the flight music.

Core sound recipes: piano, harp and celesta note samples across each instrument's range, the secret, pickup, shrine, all-shrines, ink-refill and respawn stingers, and the outdoor and hall reverb impulses.

Sound recipes for everyday effects, starting with footsteps on every surface (grass, dirt, path, sand, rock, stone, wood, water, ice, paint, snow) built from shared thud, splash, twig-snap and grunt helpers.

Sound recipes for everyday effects: footsteps, the hero's jumps, landings, glides, grabs, swim strokes, heartbeat and heavy breathing, paint throws and colour splats, fire, ice and steam, prop impacts, and UI clicks, the colour wheel and colour picks.

Sound recipes for the Painted Aerie: high wind, a distant choir and waterfalls as ambience loops, wind chimes, the area-discovery, stamina vessel and Sky Mantle stingers, snaring vines, wind gusts and storm crackle.

Every sound recipe in one list: bright sounds such as ice steps, UI clicks and chimes render at 44.1 kHz, and the list is sorted so impulse responses, UI and footsteps render first and stingers last. Also renders a recipe's variations into trimmed, normalised buffers; shared by the synth worker and the main-thread fallback.

Sound bank: renders every recipe in the synth worker, or in short main-thread slices if the worker fails, turns the results into AudioBuffers once the AudioContext exists (rendering the reverb impulse responses at its sample rate) and hands out a random variation of a sound without repeating the last one.

WebAudio engine: master compressor and limiter, the world low-pass for pause and slow motion, sfx, ambience, UI, stinger and music buses, outdoor, hall and cave reverbs, a pool of 3D voices, one-shots, pitched notes and synth pads, music ducking, the listener and a level meter. Also the looping sound used for ambience and charge hums.

Ambience: wind, rush, glide flutter, grass, surf, lake lapping, crickets, fire and slide loops follow the hero's surroundings, height, speed and the time of day, while birds, owls and frogs call from around the listener.

Hero and world sound effects driven by game events: footsteps by surface, jumps, landings, bounces, glides, climbing and swim strokes, paint throws and splats, fire, ice and steam, prop impacts, and a heartbeat and heavy breathing when health or stamina run low. Also a warn-once logger for audio errors.
Brush art sounds: the charge hum for each colour and the ready ping, casts and impacts for fireball, ice lance, bounce orb and vine lash (rising in pitch on combos), and the fizzle when ink runs out.

Battle music: its 144 BPM timing, minor-key chords and progressions, piano riff cells, accent steps and melody phrases, sequenced with taiko, shakers, pizzicato bass and piano while the hero fights, ending in a victory or escape cadence.

Battle music while enemies are alerted: a 144 BPM loop of taiko, shaker, pizzicato and piano scheduled a sixteenth at a time, heavier for brutes, with an extra layer for elites of each paint colour and a victory or escape cadence when the fight ends.

Greymaw's boss music: three phases at 84, 112 and 140 BPM with gongs, timpani, choir, brass and the stolen motifs, a victory fanfare when the boss falls, and dips or fades when the hero goes down or the fight resets.

Combat sounds: sword swings and flurries, hits coloured by the paint used, frozen foes shattering, enemy alerts, telegraphs, attacks, voices and footsteps, elite moves, the hero getting hurt or healed, pickups, lock-on, perfect dodges and the charge hum. It also starts and stops the battle music as fights begin and end.

Exploration music: a generative score that composes phrases, variations and the main motif in the mood of the moment (day, dusk, night, the Aerie, caves, the kiln, the cistern) and queues piano, harp, celesta, flute, choir and pad notes. It swells when a shrine is completed and plays the full theme once all shrines are done.

Brushflight audio: wind, flutter, boost and paint loops while flying, the hum at the summit perch that wakes once all shrines are done and fades when the brushflight is claimed, and the Skyward Stroke flight music that swells with height and speed.
Painted Aerie audio: sky wind, choir and waterfall loops that fade in as the hero reaches the sky island, wind chimes, the area discovery sting, and vine, gust and storm-crackle sounds.

Interior audio for caverns and temples: ambience loops and reverb for caves, the kiln and the cistern, with drips, chimes and pops, entry stings and the indoor music mood. It also plays the lantern hum and tinkle and the double-jump, flame-ring and frost-patch sounds.

Audio system entry: the named cues that other systems play through ctx.audio.play, and create(), which builds the engine, sound effects, ambience and music layers, wires game events to them and returns the audio API.

boss-D7QGrMym.js.header: Math helpers shared by the boss modules: clamp, smoothstep, easing curves, random ranges and angle wrapping. Also a bank of damped springs, stepped in fixed substeps, that drives Greymaw's secondary motion.

Procedural geometry for Greymaw and his arena: smooth lathes, blobs, tapered tubes, rocks and crystals. The model builder bakes vertex colour, bone skinning, drip and roughness data into one merged mesh, and small helpers compose matrices and merge or colour static parts.

Greymaw's arena in the north: a stone platform levelled above the terrain with stairs facing the summit, ruined walls with faded colour murals, pillars, braziers and rubble, merged into one stone mesh with a procedural shader. Also the swirling ink pool, the barrier wall, the storm vortex and cloud, the creeping edge ink and the arena's colliders.
The reward chest that appears in the arena once Greymaw is beaten: a wood and gold mesh with glowing gems and a hinged lid, its beam of light and rays, and its collider.

Greymaw's GPU effects: ring-buffer instance pools animated in the vertex shader (ink droplets, glows, smoke puffs, shards, ground decals, shockwave walls, colour streams and spikes). BossFx wraps them in helpers for ink and paint splashes, sparks, dust, smoke, ice shatters, landing markers, puddles and shockwaves.

The fight's gameplay hazards: expanding shockwave rings to jump over, lobbed ink globs, fire lines, ice and thorn spikes and the creeping edge ink. Each spawns its effects, damages the hero on contact and reports how soon the next threat lands.

Greymaw's procedural body: bone and part indices, body colours, and the builder that sculpts the torso, pale mask and jaw, rocky arms and fists, mane tufts, the paintbrushes on his back, ink drips and the four stolen-colour crystals into one skinned geometry with the rig's pivot, crystal, drip and surface points.

Greymaw's body material: the uniforms the boss drives each frame, the bone-skinning vertex shader with ink wobble and drips, the painted mask, jaw, stolen-colour crystals and glowing cracks in the fragment shader, a banded light ramp, and matching shadow-depth and outline materials.

Greymaw's procedural pose: 45 spring-driven channels (lean, chest, head, mask, jaw, fist targets, wrists, mane and brush sway, eye glow) composed each frame into the 14 bone matrices, with two-bone arm IK and helpers for bone, mask, mouth and crystal positions in the world.

Greymaw's tuning: phase names, the counter colour that breaks each crystal, hit-target ids and slots, health and phase thresholds, damage taken by hit source, armour, hit radii, stagger times and the mask-interrupt rule.

Greymaw, the boss: its hit targets and volumes, state machine (idle, attack, stuck, stagger, recover, phase shift), attacks per phase (slams, sweep, ink rain, crystal casts, summons) with telegraphs, damage, armour and crystal shattering, hit reactions and effects, and the uniforms it writes each frame.

The Greymaw encounter: wakes the boss when the hero reaches the arena floor, directs the rising intro, the fight and the reset after a death, the death and victory cinematics, the closing ink edge, and the grand chest that gives the Chroma Brush.
Boss system entry: builds the arena, effects, Greymaw and its encounter, exposes debug controls on window.__wbBoss, and returns the boss status other systems read.

caverns-DV9Bd1vo.js.header: Glowcap Caverns layout: chambers, tunnels, chasm, shaft, pool and pillars in cave-local coordinates, the landmark spots for chests, hints and warps, and the cave mouth on the island.

Signed-distance grid the caverns are carved from: shapes are stamped into it, sampled with trilinear filtering and meshed with surface nets. Also smooth min/max, ellipsoid and box distances and nearest-point queries on tunnel polylines.

Carves the chambers, tunnels, chasm, shaft, pool and pillars into the distance grid with noisy rock walls, meshes it, offers ground probes, and bakes ambient occlusion and fungus glow into the cave vertices.
Rock decoration geometry: wobbly stalactite and stalagmite cones, lumpy boulders, vertex welding, and the seeded random generator for the caverns.

Shared cave uniforms and the GLSL chunks patched into the cave materials: live glow lights and the awakening wave, painterly rock with lichen and crystal veins, glowing fungus, crystals, the pool and carved stone.
Builds the cave's materials by patching MeshStandardMaterial with the cave shader chunks (rock, fungus, crystal, pool, carved stone) and the additive glow-card and light-beam materials.
Glow palette and geometry builders for glowing mushrooms (stalk, cap, gills, spots) and crystal clusters, merged into single meshes with per-vertex part, cluster and glow attributes.

Scatters the cave's life and rock: glowcap clusters on floors and walls, giant grotto mushrooms, crystals, stalactites, stalagmites, boulders and hanging roots, keeping paths and puzzle spots clear, and collects the glow emitters to bake.

Carved stone props built from lathe and primitive shapes: braziers, the round brazier door with gem sockets, hint stones, the lantern altar, the Spring spiral and the root tangle, plus the ink veil material.
The cave mouth on the island: a carved rock outcrop with a tunnel, glowing fungus, a dark doorway, a hint stone and colliders, and checks for the hero standing near or inside it.
Live glow sources in the caverns (painted Ember and Frost, braziers, mushrooms, flashes): ranked and packed into shader uniforms each frame, with a few pooled point lights for the nearest.
The cave's puzzles and gates: three braziers that roll the stone door away, the giant glowcap Bloom wakes to bridge the chasm, the gloom veil, the exit portals and the shortcut roots.

Glowcap Caverns system: builds the cave, flora, glow and puzzles, registers the interior, places hints and chests, spawns the enemies and the Gloomwarden, and runs the awakening wave, warps and safety checks.

character-DjBl7MSN.js.header: The hero's skeleton: the 29 bone indices, each bone's parent and rest position, the limb lengths derived from them, bone creation, and Pose, which holds local rotations and offsets, runs forward kinematics and writes the result to the bones.

Procedural geometry for the hero: a builder that merges parts into one skinned geometry with vertex colours, up to four bone weights, a paint-tint mask and an outline width, plus loft, capsule, ellipsoid, tube, torus, vertex-weld, transform and smoothstep helpers.

The hero's body mesh: classic and sky outfit colours, skinning rules for torso, tunic, neck and head, the sculpted head with hair and hood, tunic, belt vials, satchel, arms, legs and boots, and the paintbrush, merged into one skinned geometry per outfit.

Toon shading for the hero: a banded light ramp, sun and sky rim light, paint tint and hit flash, and a dithered fade when the camera comes close, patched into standard materials. Also builds the body and inverted-hull outline materials.

The hero's face, drawn by a shader on a patch over the head: eyes that blink and look around, brows, mouth, blush and freckles, all driven by expression params. Then HeroModel, which puts together the skinned body, its outline, the face, the pose and the outfit geometries.

The Sky Mantle cape: a painted-sky shader with stars, drifting clouds, a sunset hem and the gold sun crest, on a Verlet cloth hung from the shoulders that blows in the wind, billows on demand and collides with capsules around the hero's body.

The hero's particle effects: one instanced pool of billboards for puffs, paint drops, rings, flecks, splats, impact stars and shock rings, with gravity, drag, landing on the floor and a fade for each type.
Snaring vines: leafy, thorny vines that grow up the hero's shins while slowed, sway and shed leaves as the hero moves, and burst apart when the slow wears off.
Layout of the 64 animation channels (body, two arms, two legs), the rest pose, and the spring stiffness, tracking and rate limit tuned for each channel.

Animation maths for the hero rig: a critically damped spring bank that smooths the pose channels, scalar, 3D and angle springs, and the clamp, smoothstep, pulse, envelope and easing helpers the animation code shares.

Procedural footsteps for walking, running and sprinting: each foot steps through stance and swing on a shared phase clock, lands on a probed foothold ahead of the hero with toe-off and heel-strike pitch, and the feet resettle when the hero stands still.
Two-bone IK with a soft reach limit for the arms and legs, and helpers that turn a direction plus a hint axis into a bone rotation.
Climbing limbs: plants both hands and both feet on the wall in a crawling rhythm while the hero climbs, settles the furthest one when still and swings them all up for a wall leap.
The hero's paint-splattered glider: a canopy mesh rebuilt every frame as it unfolds, billows and flutters with speed, plus the hand bar and the rigging lines.

Keyframed combat poses: the action pose (brush angle, grip, body channels, free arm, feet, lift and spin), building and sampling keyframe tracks, the guard and spin-charge stances, and the tracks for the three slashes, the spin and the jump slash.

Combat animation layer: picks the hero's current action (attack, flurry, charge, dodge, hurt, knockdown, death, victory, item reveal), poses it from the tracks or procedurally, drives the brush stroke trail and the look toward threats, and blends it over the body.

Brushflight riding pose: seats the hero on the flying brush, pitches and banks with the flight, bobs, wobbles and flinches on jolts, and poses the hands on the shaft and the legs dangling or tucked at cruising speed.

Art casting poses: the aim pose for each art (fireball, ice lance, bounce orb, vine lash) blended in while charging, keyframed cast tracks timed to each art's release, and the charge tremble, glow and shout.

Constants the hero animator shares: the locomotion modes it blends, a full turn, the pitch and yaw axes, the foot up vector and rest ankle positions, plus the scratch vectors and quaternions it reuses every frame.

The hero's procedural animator: blends ground, air, slide, swim, climb, mantle, glide and brushflight poses, layers landing, flip, aim, art, fidget, item and face overlays on top and springs the result. It then solves the legs and arms with IK, places the brush on the back or in hand, and swings the hood, satchel and fingers.

Animation preview puppet: when the player is a stub, drives its state through the animation named in the URL, or a showcase loop from idle through walk, run, sprint, jump, land, bounce, flick, slide, glide and swim to climb, along a test path, building a wall to climb and a ledge to mantle when needed.
The hero's scarf: two Verlet cloth strips anchored at the neck that flutter and whip in the wind and with speed, and collide with the body capsules and the ground.

Movement and combat effects on the hero's particle pool: surface-coloured footstep dust and flecks, landing puffs, water splashes, ripples and wakes, slide spray, paint drips and flick sprays from the brush, Spring bounce bursts, hit impacts, ground slams and charge sparks.

The Chroma Brush model: the shared rainbow palette uniform and GLSL, toon-lit shaders for its iridescent pearl handle, gold fittings, rainbow gem and streaked twinkling bristles, lathe-built parts and a dark outline shell, shown in the hero's hand.
The Chroma Brush spin wave: a rainbow ring that spreads over the terrain with a ragged curtain of colour streaking up at its front, then fades.

Brush stroke ribbons: each live stroke of the brush leaves a painterly ribbon behind the tip, smoothed with Catmull-Rom splines, that dries and fades from the tail, with dry-brush streaks at speed and rainbow colour lanes.
Afterimage ghosts of the hero: a small pool of translucent, rim-lit copies of the skinned body that freeze the current pose and fade out, left behind by dodges, perfect dodges and the flurry.
Afterimage ghosts of the hero: a small pool of translucent, rim-lit copies of the skinned body that freeze the current pose and fade out, left behind by dodges, perfect dodges and the flurry.

The gear the hero wears once found: the hip lantern that swings on a damped pendulum and lights up in the dark, the Ember and Frost Crests on the belt, and the winged Cloudstep boots that flap and puff cloud on air jumps. Also builds the gear models the prize display reuses.

Prize models for the gear items (the lantern, the Ember and Frost medals and the Cloudstep boots) that float over the hero's hands while an item is held up, then fly into their slot on the hero with a burst.

Item-get effects while the hero holds up a find: light rays behind it, the heart container crystal, the stamina vessel orb and the Sky Mantle that unfurls and swirls onto the hero, with reveal sparkles and absorb bursts.
Sky trail: the paint stroke the brush leaves behind while flying, a camera-facing ribbon smoothed with Catmull-Rom splines, with bristle streaks and dry-brush breakup, that fades with age.
Speed lines: additive streaks around the camera along the flight direction while boosting.
Bristle flare: paint-coloured strands that fan out from the brush head while flying and whip faster with speed.
Flight effects while riding the brush: drives the sky trail, speed lines and bristle flare, and emits the take-off burst, paint drips, boost spray, poured paint, water skimming and crash sparks.

Character system: builds the hero and its animator with ground and ledge probes, attaches the scarf, cape, vines, gear, glider and effects, turns combat, dodge and reward events into visuals, keeps the outfit in sync and updates it all each frame. Also drives a follow camera for the puppet stub.

content-CdF1gaAg.js.header: Site: gathers stone, prop and glyph geometry plus static colliders for one piece of world content and merges them into meshes. SiteBatch merges many sites per spatial cell, and grass clearings requested by sites are applied to vegetation in one pass.
Ruin kit: weathered stone tints and builders for columns, fallen columns, blocks, broken walls, arches, stairways, round shrine daises, hint stones, paving, rubble and the painter statue.

Smudge camps: ink stains, fire pits, ward banners, stakes, bones, ribcages and inked rocks dress each camp site, then the camp table is placed on the island, a hint stone is raised near the first camp and the enemies system spawns each camp's Smudges.
Finale: once all four Prisms blaze, coloured arcs rise from each Prism to the summit and a great rainbow unfurls over the island.
Lair hints: a hint stone near Greymaw's arena, and stones raised on the way to each elite Hoarder telling the hero which colour counters it.

Ambient wildlife: butterflies around meadows that flee the hero, birds circling landmarks and gulls over the beach, dragonflies along the lake shore, and fish that leap from the lake with splashes and ripples.

Content materials: weathered stone with moss, grime and old paint stains, hand-made props, and glowing glyphs drawn from a procedural glyph atlas whose glow follows island vitality or per-site glow slots.
Trial Prism: a floating faceted crystal with a halo, a light beam and a ground ring. It sits dormant, charges when the trial is won, then bursts and blazes in its colour.
Perch parts: layout constants, hint texts, easing helpers, shaders and geometry for the summit Perch: the petals of the stone bud, the Skybrush relic and its feathered wings, and the socket prongs.

The Painter's Perch on the summit: a socket for each colour lights up as its trial is won, and once all four are lit the stone bud opens, a pillar of light rises and the Skybrush floats up. Runs the awakening and claiming cinematics and the prompt to take up the Skybrush, which grants brushflight.
Bramble gate: a thorny procedural thicket that bars the canyon into the grove. Only red paint or fire burns it; it chars, glows with embers and dissolves away.
Cliff vines: leafy strands, with the odd flower, hung down the cliff faces around a point and swaying in the wind.

The four colour trials: Bloom on the mesa, Frost on the lake islet, Spring at the ruined tower and Ember in the grove behind the bramble gate. Builds each trial's ruins, hint stones, ink plants, warp point and Prism, shows the prompt to touch a dormant Prism and completes the trial when it is touched.
The painter's camp beside the spawn point: fire ring, log seat, easel with a half-finished painting, crate of paint pots, brush jar, bedroll, tent, paintings drying on a line and a lantern post.

World dressing around the island: the painter's camp and its hint stone, ruins (a north arch, the painter statue, a colonnade, beach and lake-house ruins, summit stairs, a forest ring and a lookout), scattered ink plants, mote areas and meadows. Also builds the physics playground near spawn with a ramp, a platform, crates, barrels, a ball and a boulder.

Content system: builds the trials, the Perch, the smudge camps and the world dressing, and wires trial completion to toasts, events, the Perch and the finale. Applies the trials, perch and warp URL presets and updates all content each frame.

debug-BrTCcdHg.js.header: Audio test panel, opened with ?audiotest: a button for every named sound and every footstep, hero, paint, combat, brush art, enemy, boss, flight, area and ambience cue, toggles for the audio overrides, an hour slider, music and volume controls, and a live readout of the audio engine.

elements-Dqrzpsbu.js.header: Shader chunk wb_burn_pars that lets terrain and plants read the fire burn map: patchy charred scorch marks with a warm rim, and the flickering glow of smouldering ground.
Scripted element showcases for the elementsdemo URL parameter (a burning dry meadow, a campfire, painted props, a lakeshore with ice floes and steam), with the camera framing used for screenshots.
Shared helpers for the element effects: particle budgets per quality setting, the tiling noise texture used by flames, smoke, ice and props, the fog GLSL helper, and small random and hash functions.

Fire simulation on a 1 m grid: grass, trees and flammable objects heat up, catch and spread with wind and slope, burn out into the burn map and regrow later. Heat is pooled into blocks that drive updrafts, smoke, embers and the flickering fire lights.
Instanced billboard flames with a noise-carved flame-tongue shader, refilled every fire tick from burning ground and trees, plus fixed slots for burning props.
Frost ice floes that freeze on water: faceted floe meshes with a glassy, frosted ice shader and walkable kinematic colliders that bob, then crack and sink, or melt under fire.
GPU particle pools animated in the vertex shader: soft, sun-lit puffs for smoke and steam, and additive glows for embers, sparks and glitter.
One-shot element effects built from puffs and glows: steam, sizzle, sparks, ignition bursts, ember puffs, frost, ice shards and the green bloom.
RoundedBoxGeometry (the three.js addon): a box with rounded edges and corners and continuous UVs, used to build the crate.

Paintable physics props (crate, barrel, boulder, ball): red sets wood alight and makes stone red-hot, blue frosts them and makes them slippery, yellow makes them bouncy, green sprouts grass tufts, and water floats wood and puts fires out.

Elements system: creates fire, flames, ice, props and effects, turns paint splats into burning, dousing, freezing and regrowth, and exposes ignite, extinguish, freezeWater, updraftAt and spawnProp to the other systems.

enemies-C9evYR9S.js.header: Smudge definitions: base stats for the smudgeling, spitter and brute, every attack's timings and damage, the paint statuses and their tuning, and the elite (Hoarder, Thornmother, Galecaller), Stormborne and AI tuning.
Populates the Painted Aerie once the hero gets near: its two sky elite arenas (Thornmother and Galecaller), the camps at its pack spots and a few wandering Smudges.
Instanced spikes that elites raise from the ground (ice, thorns, cinder, spring crystal) with their shader; each spike pops up, lingers and reports when it expires.
Additive light columns for elites: the beacon over an arena's hoard, erupting geysers and the pillars over dropped hearts, with swirling colour ribbons.
The glowing hearts a defeated elite leaves behind: an extruded heart shape with a rainbow-swirled material, instanced.

Elite arenas: for each Hoarder a ring of standing stones, masked totems, banners, crystals and the hoard pile with its beacon, painted ground and colliders. Spawns the elite and its escorts, warps the hero there for testing and celebrates when it falls.
The Enemy record: per-Smudge state for AI, physics, statuses and animation, plus the damped spring bank and the channel indices that drive its procedural pose.
Procedural Smudge meshes: a skinned-geometry builder with bone, part and drip attributes, and the smudgeling, spitter and brute bodies with masks, limbs, drips, elite crowns and cloud mantles.
Smudge rendering: skinning, face, crack and toon-lighting GLSL, the body, shadow and outline materials, and the per-kind instanced renderer that reads bones and look parameters from a float texture.

Procedural Smudge animation: sets spring targets each frame for gait, looking at the hero, idle fidgets and every state (notice, telegraph, attack, recover, stagger, flee, dying, statuses), then steps the springs.

Turns an enemy's animated pose channels into bone matrices for its parts (body, top, mask, hands, feet and the kind-specific extra), packs them with the shading parameters into the instance texture, and maps rig points such as the mouth or fists to world space.

Smudge camps: builds the merged prop mesh (fire ring, ash, logs, mask cairn and banner pole) with a tattered, burnable ink banner, adds colliders, places the camp members around the fire, and burns the banner when it is ignited.

GPU particle effects for enemies: ring-buffer instanced pools for ink droplets, glows, puffs, ice and ink shards, ground decals and shock waves, each with its own shader, plus the EnemyFx facade (ink and paint splashes, sparks, dust, smoke, ice shatter, rings, markers, puddles, sector warnings).

Attacks of the Painted Aerie's elites: the Thornmother's vine whip, thorn eruptions and root grab lanes, and the Galecaller's gusts, gale ring, wind ride and bouncing orbs, with their telegraphs, hit checks and the vines that bind the hero.
Stormborne (tier 2) Smudges: violet crackle, sparks and arcs around them, and the lightning discharge ring they release when they die.

Elite Hoarders: per-enemy elemental state and the controller for their charge, slam, backhand, volley, spikes, nova, pound and lunge attacks, fire patches, rings and eruptions, auras, death burst and the heart container they drop.

Ink globs lobbed by spitters and their elite and storm variants: ballistic flight with dripping trails and a landing marker, melee swings that reflect them back at their owner, bouncing orbs, and the ink splat where they land.
Heart and ink pickups dropped by defeated Smudges: they pop out, settle and bob on the ground, drift toward the nearby hero and heal or refill ink when collected.
Status visuals drawn over Smudges, each as one instanced batch: flame tongues while burning, a cracking ice shell while frozen, and vines that grow around them while rooted.

Enemy director: spawns Smudges and their camps, runs their senses and AI states (idle, wander, notice, engage, telegraph, attack, flee, search, return), hands out attack tokens, applies damage and paint statuses, moves them with Rapier character controllers, and plays their deaths, loot drops and ambient ink effects.

Enemies system entry: builds the director, a registry of external lock-on targets such as boss parts, the elite arenas and the Aerie encounter, handles debug spawns from the URL and exposes the spawn, query, damage, hitSphere and lock-on API.

paint-DPWlG1ZU.js.header: Blob ballistics: steps a thrown ink blob along its gravity arc and stops it at the first collider or water surface it crosses. Used for blobs in flight and for the throw preview.

Shared paint constants: the paint volume layout (voxel size, brick grid, atlas slots, indirection layers), the vitality map bounds, blob and splat radii, and each ink's channel and colour, with a helper that writes a colour as a GLSL vec3.

Paint demo (debug panel button or ?paintdemo=1, wall, nowall or loop): throws blobs of all four inks from the camera onto the ground, a stone test wall and nearby water, then blooms vitality around the target.

The wb_paint_pars GLSL chunk that lets any material show paint: volume lookup, the four ink surface styles (Ember cracks, Frost facets, Spring ripples, Bloom leaves and vines), splatter droplets and relief, and the vitality fade and bloom-wave glow. Also builds the tiling 3D noise texture the chunk samples.
patchMaterial: hooks a three.js standard, physical, Lambert, Phong or toon material's onBeforeCompile so its fragment shader gets the world position and applies paint and vitality from wb_paint_pars.

Splatter: writes paint into the volume as noisy spheres, tapered capsules and directional splats with lobed outlines, satellite drops and streaks, erases paint, and runs the drips that crawl down steep surfaces.
Throw preview: glowing beads flowing along the predicted blob arc and a pulsing ring of dashes where the blob will land.

Splash effects: an instanced droplet mesh (wobbling teardrops, landing pancakes, glassy water spray), the simulation that moves and recycles the droplets, and the ripple, foam and dye rings left on water.
Additive sparkle points (star glints, rising embers, soft motes) with drag and buoyancy, used for each ink's landing sparkles and the glitter along bloom waves.

Vitality map: a 512 by 512 texture of how alive the land is, from faded watercolour to vivid colour. Bloom waves restore it in expanding rings and feed their glowing fronts to shaders, drain clears it, and changes upload as dirty rectangles.

Paint volume: sparse 3D paint coverage with one RGBA channel per ink, kept as 8-voxel bricks with a one-voxel apron in a 3D texture atlas plus an indirection table. Paints and erases through coverage functions, samples on the CPU, evicts the least recently painted bricks and uploads changes to the GPU on a budget.

Paint system (ctx.paint): the four inks and their regeneration, thrown blobs and what happens when they land (splats, splashes, sparkles, bloom), the trajectory preview, and the API for sampling, painting, erasing, vitality and patching materials.

player-BWE2CXZl.js.header: Physics probes shared by the hero, the camera and the brush: Rapier ray casts that report the hit point, normal and collider, and sphere casts that report the distance to the first hit, skipping sensors and an excluded collider.

Hero tuning table: capsule size, running, sprinting and turning, jumps and air control, gliding, climbing and mantling, swimming, sliding, yellow-paint bounces, stamina costs, brushflight handling and the follow camera.

Third-person camera rig: orbits the hero with mouse or stick look, drifts behind the run direction, frames the lock-on target, pulls back for speed, gliding and brushflight, keeps clear of walls and the ground, adds shake, landing dip, hit punch and kick, and blends into scripted cinematic shots.

Hero movement on a Rapier kinematic character controller: running with skids and sprint, coyote and buffered jumps, air jumps, sliding on ice and blue paint, yellow-paint bounces, gliding on updrafts, climbing green paint, vaulting and mantling ledges, swimming, brushflight with crashes, stamina, slows, and respawning at the last safe spot.

Brush melee combat: the slash combo, jump slash and charged spin (with the chroma brush's rainbow paint wave), hits on enemies and props along the brush's sweep, painting ground slams, dodges and the perfect-dodge masterstroke flurry, lock-on, hit feedback and rumble, and taking damage, dying and respawning.

Training dummies for the ?dummy URL flag: a row of straw targets on wooden posts that stands in for the enemies system. They wobble and flash when struck, can wind up and swing back at the hero, and pop back up a few seconds after being knocked down.

The hero's items and upgrades: which ones are owned, the perks they give (extra hearts and stamina, the Sky Mantle's lighter drain, Cloudstep's air jump), and the item-get moment that freezes time, frames the hero holding the item up with a camera shot and then grants it.

Painting with the brush: switches the selected colour, turns the hero toward the aim point, flicks ink blobs along the paint system's launch arc (leading the shot while flying), pours a stream of ink during brushflight and casts the aim ray behind the reticle.

One instanced particle pool for every brush-art effect: flames, smoke, sparks, ice shards, stars, leaves, ground rings, shockwaves, glows, paint drops, mist, embers and snowflakes, each with its own look in a shared shader.

Meshes and shaders for the brush arts: comet-tailed fireballs, faceted ice lances, jiggling bounce orbs, ribbon trails, leafy vine lashes and their thorns, and the dashed line that previews an art's flight path. Also the colours, random helpers and scratch objects the art effects share.

Brush art visuals: the charge glow and the art held at the brush tip, the aim arc and landing marker, the fireball, ice lance, bounce orb and vine lash in flight, and their bursts, shatters, bounces, vine grabs, ladder dabs and thorn patches.
Crest upgrade effects: the ring of fire an Ember Crest fireball leaves on the ground and the ice crystals a Frost Crest lance grows along its path.

Brush arts: hold paint to charge the selected colour's art and release it as a fireball, ice lance, bounce orb or vine lash. Steps the projectiles and vines (enemy grabs, wall ladders, thorn patches), soft-aims at enemies, previews the path, deals damage and paint, and applies the Ember and Frost Crest upgrades.
Player system entry: builds the controller, camera rig, painter, combat, items and brush arts, applies URL debug options and returns the player API that runs every frame.

render-Bg7DJhwm.js.header: Atmosphere particles: wind-blown dust motes by day and blinking fireflies at dusk, drawn as point clouds that wrap around the camera and follow the terrain.
Height fog: replaces three.js fog shader chunks with distance haze, analytic height fog and sun-scattered fog colour, and injects the shared fog uniforms into every material.
Tileable Perlin and Worley noise baked into the RGBA noise texture that the sky and cloud shaders sample.
Base Pass class of the bundled postprocessing library and the simple passes built on it: fullscreen triangle, clear-mask, copy, clear and stencil mask passes.
EffectComposer with its timer: owns the ping-pong render targets and depth texture and runs the post-processing pass chain each frame.
Effect base class with its attributes, shader sections, shader data, blend functions and blend modes, plus the Resolution helper and the override-material manager used by passes.
Bloom: luminance threshold, Kawase and mipmap blur passes and the BloomEffect that adds the blurred highlights back over the image.
ShaderPass runs a fullscreen material; RenderPass draws the scene into the composer's buffer with optional override material, selection and background skipping.
SMAA anti-aliasing: edge detection and blend-weight materials, lookup images and the SMAAEffect that combines them.
EffectPass merges several effects into one EffectMaterial shader, prefixing each effect's uniforms and functions, and renders it as a single fullscreen pass.
Unused lookup tables left behind by the bundled postprocessing library: tetrahedral LUT corners and SMAA area-texture subsample offsets and edge patterns.

Start of the vendored N8AO ambient occlusion library: the fullscreen triangle its passes draw with and the AO shader that samples a hemisphere around each pixel against the depth buffer. It opens with the last SMAA search-texture helpers of the postprocessing library.
N8AO's compositing shader, which blends the denoised ambient occlusion into the frame with depth-aware upsampling, an AO tint, fog and transparency awareness, and the debug display modes.
N8AO's bundled int8 neural denoise model, checked at load, and the GLSL generated from its weights: token layers, attention query scores, the summary head and the output.
N8AO's denoise shader: a depth- and normal-aware Poisson-disk blur of the raw ambient occlusion, with the optional neural denoise path.
N8AO's half-resolution pass, which downsamples scene depth and reconstructs normals so ambient occlusion can run at half resolution.

The N8AO post pass that gives the island its soft ambient occlusion: a configuration proxy, the AO, denoise and composite passes, quality presets and transparency handling. Also holds the blue-noise bits, a multi-render-target compat class, the GPU timer helper and the depth-buffer type enum.
The game's post-processing chain: N8AO, bloom, light shafts with drifting cloud shadows and ink outlines, a painterly grade with AgX, ACES or neutral tone mapping, SMAA and the paper-grain finish.
The sky dome: zenith-to-horizon gradient, twilight belt, sun halo and disc, stars, moon, overhead cloud puffs and the horizon cumulus band, updated every frame from the time-of-day sky and the wind.
Hand-tuned sky keyframes across the 24-hour day and the sun and moon paths, blended into one sky state of colours, light intensities, fog, stars and exposure.

The environment system (ctx.environment): hemisphere and sun or moon lights with a texel-snapped shadow camera, fog, wind, the day cycle, quality and dynamic resolution, the post chain and the final render. setInterior blends to cave and temple lighting.

sky-B7wRjF5B.js.header: Collects the stone, glass and rock pieces of the sky's structures with their collider descriptions, then merges each kind into one static mesh and registers the colliders.
Cloud, mist, smoke and steam puffs around the sky isles, drawn as one billboard mesh whose shader drifts, swells and fades them, and thins them out near the camera.

The sky's vitality map: how much colour each spot has regained, restored in spreading prismatic waves when paint lands or foes fall. Also the GLSL that greys out drained ground and the skyify patch that adds it to a material.
A baked texture over the isles holding ground height, grass density and tree canopy, which the grass and flower shaders sample.

Flora of the sky isles: GPU-placed rings of grass and six kinds of wildflower that sway in the wind, part around the hero and take paint, plus instanced blossom, birch, pine and oak trees with trunk colliders.
One floating isle: a noisy outline, a domed top with flats, bumps and paths, a lobed rocky underside and splat weights, with fast height, rim and underside queries.
Layout of the Painted Aerie: its five isles (the Aerie, Stepstone, Cascade, Stormcrag and Highwind Perch) and the named spots for the landing, shrine, foes and chests.
Shaders and materials for the sky isles, their stonework and their stained glass: meadow, snow, volcanic and lush ground, bump detail and glowing veins, all faded by vitality.
Building blocks for the Aerie's ruins: stone, paint and pastel palettes, and geometry for faceted tiers, tapered blocks, crystals, gems and voussoir arches.

Ruins of the Painted Aerie: the undersides of every isle (stalactites, roots, hanging crystals, floating debris), the main isle's tiered temple with stairs, lens obelisks, colonnade, easel circle and rose gate, and the stepstone, cascade, stormcrag and highwind ruins. Also collects the platforms, falls, pools, trees and ink plants they add.
Sky waterfalls and pools: one mesh of falling sheets, the streams that feed them and flat pools, with a shader for flutter, foam and ripples. Returns mist points for the clouds at each fall.

Base class for the sky realms beyond the Aerie (Canopy Isle, Cinder Isle and Frostspire): builds their isle shapes, colliders, chests, ink plants, water, clouds, motes and flora, tracks walkable surfaces, puzzles and enemy groups, and announces the realm when the hero lands on it.

Geometry helpers shared by the realms: paint colours, lathed peaks from a height profile, paths with closest-point and height queries, profile sweeps, fall sheets, icicles, shatter facets, ropes and paint runes, plus tagging parts for the dyn material.

Realm materials: the dyn feature material (per-part roughness, metalness and glow with vitality), lava with freezable sections and a curtain, the ice shell that cracks and shatters, and swaying painterly leaves.

Canopy Isle realm: the great tree with roots, decks, crow's nest bridge and crown shrine; three buds woken with Bloom grow vine ladders and leaf steps, a Spring blossom bounces the hero, and the Lost Hue leads to its hoard in the Hollow Stump.

Cinder Isle, the volcanic side realm: a crater cone pours lava into a moat around the Ember Vault and out over the edge in lavafalls. Frost paint or an Ice Lance cools a lava section into obsidian crust for a while, so the hero can cross it and crumble the vault's lava curtain; spitters on basalt ledges and the Magmite elite guard the isle.

Frostspire and its little Floe islet: Frost paint glazes the Frost Run chute spiralling down the peak into ice for sliding, and the Frozen Giant's four seals must be melted with Ember in the order the obelisks show before it wakes and gives up its heart container.

Sky system entry: builds the Painted Aerie (isles, ruins, water, clouds, flora, colliders, chests and ink plants) and its side realms, unseals the grand chest once both sky elites fall, and handles warps and realm respawns. Every frame it updates the realms and hides what is far from the camera.

temples-B-TGmSpf.js.header: Temple stone material: the surface kinds (ashlar, smooth, metal, basalt, ice, wood, glass, rough) and the shader chunks that give a standard material sixteen temple point lights, glyph glow channels, frost and soot themes and the glow once the temple is lit.
Temple glyphs: the rune atlas drawn on a canvas (flame, snowflake, key, ring, drop, sun, mask and random runes) and the decal material that lights each glyph by its channel.
Temple effect materials: flowing lava, freezable water, billboard flames, heat columns, light shafts, portal surfaces and ice that grows out from a point.

TempleKit, the builder for temple interiors: floors, ceilings, walls with doorways and trim, pilasters, columns, basalt, stairs, braziers, hint stones, glyphs and lava, merged into meshes with static colliders. Also the room, glyph frieze and banner helpers.
Shared helpers for temple props (merged meshes, boxes, sounds, colliders), the temple light rig, sliding doors (stone, bars, locked and boss doors) and the braziers that Ember lights.
Ink webs that block temple passages until Ember burns them away: strands, thorns and eyes, charring, embers and the dissolve.
Temple devices: the Small Key pickup, ink fonts that refill paint, the hot-air vent that lifts the hero, pressure plates and portals.

Temple chests (small, key and grand): parts built per style, lids hinged in the shader, the open prompt and the opening cinematic with rays and bursts, and the rewards (an item, a full ink cache, hearts or a Small Key).

Temple encounters: battle rooms that seal their doors and send waves of Smudges until cleared, and the boss fight with its intro cinematic, hazards, win and reset. Also the sleep helper and scratch vector the temple uses.

Temple base class shared by every Paint Temple: registers the interior and builds the common pieces (doors, braziers, ink webs, ink fonts, sconces, light shafts, hint stones, chests, portals). Tracks Small Keys and locked doors, checkpoints and safe ground, and lights the temple up once its crest is claimed.

The Frozen Cistern, the Frost temple: palette, spec and layout. Freeze the channel and the cascade, slip through the timed ice gate, thaw the key with Ember, clear the guard room and outlast the Rimewarden's falling icicles.

Temple gates on the island: a yaw-rotated build kit and the Kiln and Cistern gateways set into the terrain, with steps down to the ground, braziers, a heat column, motes and the portal that travels inside.
Small Key counter: the pill near the top-left of the screen showing how many keys the hero carries inside a temple.

The Kiln, the Ember temple: palette, spec and layout. Wake the entry braziers, burn the ink webs, ride the heat vent up to the key ledge, clear the guard room and dodge Kilnheart's erupting fire vents.

Paint Temples system: creates the Kiln, the Frozen Cistern and their gates, routes paint splats and combat hits to the active temple, and handles the temple and warp URL parameters and the key counter.

terrain-KTXjirmi.js.header: Generates the island heightmap on a 321 by 321 grid from signed-distance landforms: coastline and sea cliffs, the summit and its ridges, the south slope, mesa, tower hill, canyon, grove, lake and islet, rock spires, sea stacks and dirt paths. Also bakes the masks the surface pass needs and exports the key plateau heights.
Turns the heightmap into vertex normals, two splat-weight maps, a surface type per cell (grass, dirt, sand, rock, path or snow) and a grass density map.

The terrain material: a standard material patched with painterly splat shading for grass, golden grass, dirt, sand, paths, rock strata, sandstone and snow, plus relief bumps, underwater caustics and burn marks.
Distant scenery: low-poly islands on the horizon, lit by the sun and hazed toward the fog colour.

The terrain system: generates the island, builds the chunked terrain mesh, the Rapier heightfield and the height texture, and answers height, normal, surface and grass-density queries and landmark positions.

ui-B6m58HFF.js.header: Canvas brush kit behind the painterly UI: bristle brush strokes along a smoothed path, ink splats with tendrils and drops, brush rings, watercolour washes, paper grain and rough paper cards. Also the stroke, splat, ring and wash canvases the widgets are built from, and hex colour helpers.

Painted HUD art: the heart curve and the layered heart sprites (back, fill, ghost, outline, splash), crack lines for broken hearts, and cached painted screen vignettes. Also the inked SVGs for the lock-on arrow and ring, the alert marks and the sparkle.
DOM helpers for the HUD widgets: create an element in one call, and set a style, text or class only when it actually changes.
Inked SVG icons: the element icon for each paint colour (flame, snowflake, spring, leaves), the Prism Trial gem, the mouse and the check mark.

Lock-on HUD: the spinning ring and head marker over the locked enemy, with its health bar (draining ghost, ticks, elite name and colour) and status icons, plus floating bars over nearby alerted brutes and elites. Also projects world points to the screen and looks enemies up by id.
Alert marks over enemies: a yellow ! pops up when a Smudge notices the hero and a ? when it gives up the chase, following the enemy on screen.

Area title cards: entering a named area spells its name out letter by letter between painted rules, tinted for caves, kilns, cisterns, temples and the sky island, and the same area is not announced again for 40 seconds.
The Solved! card shown when a puzzle is solved: a painted ring with a brush-stroke check mark, ink spots and sparks, coloured for the area it was solved in.

Brush Art charge meter: a ring that fills while the hero holds to charge, with the art's name, its ink cost and a ready notch. It shakes when there is not enough ink, bursts in the art's colour on a cast and puffs grey when the cast fizzles.
First-time Brush Art tips: hold to charge, then release to cast each colour's art, remembered in localStorage once learned.
Full-screen combat effects: painted vignettes for getting hurt and for low health, the Masterstroke banner and strike prompt after a perfect dodge (and its flurry), and the death screen.
Combat tutorial prompts: lock on, strike, charge a spin and dodge, each shown once at the right moment in a fight and remembered in localStorage.

The four Prism Trials (Ember, Frost, Spring, Bloom): where each shrine stands, a tracker of which are complete, and the HUD row of prisms that fill in, with a prism flying into place when a trial is won.

Compass strip at the top of the screen: headings and ticks scroll with the camera, with marks and distances for the trial shrines, Greymaw's arena, the sky island, the brush perch, entrances already found and nearby elites.
Flight HUD while riding the brush: altitude and speed readouts, and speed lines at the screen edges that grow with speed and boosting, tinted by the selected colour.
Flight tutorial: steps the player through steering, rising and diving, boosting, painting from the air and dismounting, moving on as each is done, shown only once.
Crosshair in the middle of the screen that opens into an inked aiming reticle in the selected colour while the hero aims.
Toast queue: titled cards with a painted stroke in the toast's colour (rainbow when it has none) and ink dots, shown one after another.
Key prompts: painted pills with a key cap, a line of text and an optional subline, shown and hidden by id; key codes are turned into short labels.
Controls hint panel listing the keys (move, look, jump, strike, aim, lock on, colours, interact), with the Ride the brush row unlocked once the hero can fly. The list is shared with the pause menu.

Full-screen overlays: the fade to and from black, whose promise resolves when it ends, and the Click to take control notice shown while the pointer is free. Also the heart limits (at most 20 hearts, 10 per row) and quarter-heart rounding used by the hearts row.
Heart row in the HUD: painted hearts fill and drain by quarters behind a lagging ghost, crack and splash on damage, sparkle when healed or when a new heart is gained, and beat when health runs low.
Ink palette: a glass jar for each paint colour whose liquid tracks the hero's ink, with the selected colour's name, a cost preview while an art charges, and flashes when ink runs out or is refilled.
Pause menu on a painted paper card with Journal (Prism Trials), Brush Arts, Settings and Controls tabs; settings are edited in place and saved.
Painted canvas icons for the Glowcap Lantern, the Ember and Frost Crests and the Cloudstep Boots, with sparkle, glow and gold-gradient helpers.
Rainbow gradient and rainbow brush-stroke helpers, and painted canvas icons for the Heart of Colour, the Chroma Brush, Brushflight, the Stamina Vessel and the Sky Mantle.
Item banner: when the hero gets an item, a painted card shows its icon, title, description and a tip with key caps, timed to the item hold-up pose.
Boss HUD: the boss's title card, then a health bar with a lagging ghost and phase pips; plus the smaller banner that announces elite foes.
Stamina ring floating beside the hero's head: a vine-wreathed dial that drains and refills, extra segmented rings from Stamina Vessels, and a badge while the hero is slowed.
Title screen: the WILDBRUSH logo over paint splats and a brush swash, the tagline, and click, Enter or Space to begin with an ink burst.
Colour wheel: hold Tab to slow time and pick a paint with the mouse, look input or number keys; shows each colour's ink level and element.
The UI system: builds the HUD layers and overlays, runs the title, pause and colour-wheel flows, routes game events to the widgets, and exposes toasts, prompts and fades.

vegetation-BAJ8ooGY.js.header: The vegetation field: terrain height, grass density, dryness, canopy shade and slope baked on a grid over the island and uploaded as a float texture that grass, flowers and rocks sample in their shaders. Grass can be cleared from discs of it and trees splat their shade into it.

Wildflowers: daisies, buttercups, poppies, lavender, cornflowers and pink blooms drawn as instanced rings that follow the camera. The vertex shader places them in patches, picks the species and bends them with the wind and the hero.
Grass: rings of instanced curved blades that follow the camera. The vertex shader clumps them, bends them with gusts and the hero, and tints them by dryness, paint and fire.
Groups instance matrices by material and builds one BatchedMesh per material when multi-draw is available, otherwise one InstancedMesh per geometry.
Small plants: bushes, ferns, reeds with cattails, lily pads and mushrooms, built from seeds and scattered over the island by the placement rules.
Rocks and pebbles: noisy faceted rock meshes with moss and sand shading, scattered over the island; the bigger ones get convex-hull colliders.

Trees: picks spots and species (broadleaf, conifer, birch, palm) by biome, batches tinted trunks and foliage, adds trunk colliders and canopy shade, and keeps a spatial hash for finding trees near a point.
Placement rules shared by trees, plants and rocks: clearings around landmarks and the boss arena, the canyon corridor, paths, the terrain surface and the dry meadow.

The vegetation system: bakes the field, builds trees, rocks, plants, grass and flowers, switches grass and flower quality with the settings, and answers trees-near-a-point and grass-clearing requests.

water-DvAoIGJY.js.header: The water shader and material: wind-aligned waves that fade with depth, calmer lake water, fresnel sky reflection, sun glints, shoreline foam and a dim view from below the surface.
The water system: the sea mesh (a dense grid around the island plus a flat skirt out to the horizon), the underwater screen tint, and water depth queries.

headers.synth.worker-uMR_s6Wv.js:
Sound synthesis worker: on a 'render' message it renders every procedural sound recipe offline, in priority order and skipping ids already cached, and posts each finished sound back with its sample buffers transferred.
Holds the whole synth: seeded RNG and id hashing, state-variable and one-pole filters, pink and brown noise, tones, filtered noise, modal pings, grains and crackles, piano, harp, celesta and bell notes, brass, pads, choir and formant voices, echo taps and impulse responses.
Recipes cover ambience, critters, combat, the Greymaw fight, caverns, movement, painting, music and UI; each sound is conditioned, trimmed or crossfade-looped, then normalised.
